baseline_comparison.scope: Same final common people for individual baselines; official national copy is a separate population/metric.

dispersion.center: Same-person current human Q9 density-mean median, not the official national headline
dispersion.aggregation: Design-weighted within month; average statistics over two repeats, then equal months
limits: A larger variance cannot rule out memorized headlines, distributions or related macro facts.
A small variance or central clustering cannot establish memorization; shared information can also cause it.
Between-person spread, within-person generation noise and subjective Q9 uncertainty are distinct.
Only two repeats; variance subtraction is descriptive and may be negative.
Same inputs change both served model and provider; this is not a parameter-count-only experiment.

q9_postprocessing.coverage_semantics: Original plus resumed raw call ledger. Failed calls stay missing; analysis uses normalized Q9.

limits: Four later-2025 months are not proof of absence of pretraining contamination; aggregates were public before model release.
Model cutoff evidence incomplete; no strict-B claim. True own prior and current demographic profiles are declared A-line inputs.
National food-category proxies and synthetic ATUS2022 role/CE2020Q4/Fed-confidence remain measurement approximations.
National/cohort baseline results inspected before this batch, but no model responses or outcomes used for roster selection; no global blind-test claim.
Repeated generations are within-person randomness, not extra independent people. No automatic default upgrade.
correction_note: v1 derived national fields reconstructed a center from the equal-person branch plus weighted real center. Use this cached weighted readout; no calls, density fits, truths, prompts or primary weighting changed. Detected before new results were inspected.

support_sensitivity.note: Primary complete-repeat support is unchanged. Separate-repeat supports differ. The fixed-roster option keeps every human-valid person and substitutes only a scalar prior when a model response/score is missing; it is a post-hoc deployment diagnostic, not an LLM reply or newly passed primary test.
